scenario: [RDSC.5a.8.1]: the runtime keys the state it allocates on the whole tuple, the atom included. `mean all_time` (SeriesBackendWelfordEwma) and `p50 sample 4` (SeriesBackendReservoir) on one slot both declare window 0, so only the atom tells their rows apart. Six samples, 10.0 five times then 70.0 (each a new `n`, so each a sample), then a `Probe` reads both. `mean` is the running mean of all six, 20.0. `p50` is the reservoir's: any four of the six hold at most one 70.0, so the interpolated median is 10.0 whichever four Algorithm R keeps ([LSMP.2.1]). A runtime keying the state on the window alone gives the two backings one row, and the mean reads the reservoir's four samples, 10.0 or 25.0. Path: libds one `backend_state` per backend slot, and `series_pick_backend_slot`, which takes SeriesBackendWelfordEwma for an unbounded `mean`; Mercury `ds.series` `row_key` and `read_backing`.
rules_ds:
use default

schema Reading scope logical:
    dev: String key
    level: Float mutable
    n: Int mutable

schema Probe scope explicit:
    k: Int

series Reading.level:
    mean all_time
    p50 sample 4

rule read:
    Probe
    Reading r
->
    log info "{r.mean} {r.p50}"
